_what: Hand-written notes about bills that recur under the same number every term. Edited by a person; no generator writes this file. Keyed by bill number WITHOUT a term, because the whole point is that HB1 is the budget in every term rather than in one -- which is the opposite of how the rest of this project keys things, and is why it is a separate file rather than a field on a bill.

_fields.from: First filing year the note applies to. Bills of that number BEFORE this year are different bills that happen to share it, and get no note.
_fields.chamber: H or S, so HB1 and SB1 cannot be confused.
_fields.label: A short name for the bill's role, shown as a heading.
_fields.note: The explanation, in the project's own words. Plain English, no markup.
_fields.checked: When a person last read this and agreed with it.

_verified: HB1 exists from 1989 but the 1989 and 1991 bills are not budgets -- 1989 HB1 is a special session bill about public utilities commission approval, and 1991 HB1 is a medicaid enhancement tax. The appropriations title begins in 1993, which is why 'from' is 1993 for both and not 1989.

notes.label: The state budget
notes.note: HB 1 is the core financial spreadsheet of the state budget, filed alongside HB 2 in the first year of the term. It outlines the exact line-item spending for public services, healthcare, infrastructure, and state agencies for a two-year period.

notes.label: The budget trailer bill
notes.note: HB 2 is known as the budget trailer bill, filed alongside HB 1 in the first year of the term. Because HB 1 only specifies monetary amounts, HB 2 contains the statutory law changes, fee adjustments, and policy language needed to execute and pay for that spending. HB 2 can make changes to state tax structures, raise or lower state fees, and update funding formulas. HB 2 may also contain policy items not directly related to the budget through amendments.
